sections.title: Comparing similarities
sections.content:
Ways to show things are similar:
• likewise — in the same way. She is talented; likewise, her brother is gifted.
• correspond to — be equivalent to. Their findings correspond to our own research.
• akin to — similar to. The experience was akin to flying.
• analogous — comparable in certain respects. The human brain is often described as analogous to a computer.
• parallel — occurring at the same time in a similar way. There are obvious parallels between the two cases.

sections.title: Showing contrasts
sections.content:
Ways to highlight differences:
• whereas — in contrast. She prefers coffee, whereas he drinks tea.
• on the contrary — the opposite is true. He isn't lazy; on the contrary, he works extremely hard.
• conversely — introducing an opposing point. Rich nations produce more waste; conversely, poorer nations produce less.
• nevertheless — despite that. The task was difficult; nevertheless, she completed it perfectly.
• distinct from — clearly different. This approach is distinct from traditional methods.

exercises.question: 'Akin to' means:
exercises.explanation: Akin to means of similar character or nature.

exercises.question: 'Nevertheless' is closest in meaning to:
exercises.explanation: Nevertheless means in spite of that; notwithstanding.

exercises.question: 'Whereas' is used to show:
exercises.explanation: Whereas introduces a contrast between two facts or ideas.

exercises.question: Two things that are comparable in certain ways are:
exercises.explanation: Analogous means comparable in certain respects, typically in a way that helps explanation.

exercises.question: 'On the contrary' is used when:
exercises.explanation: On the contrary means the opposite of what has been stated is true.

exercises.question: 'Conversely' introduces:
exercises.explanation: Conversely introduces a statement that reverses the previous one.

exercises.question: 'Likewise' means:
exercises.explanation: Likewise means in the same way; also.

exercises.question: Something clearly different from another thing is:
exercises.explanation: Distinct from means clearly different or separate.
